policy: vanilla -> official REDmod -> Biology-owned narrow scripting -> generic extension only when necessary

dependencies.rationale: Official package/deployment authority for the REDmod-first release.

consumerFeatures: native hook seams listed in manifest/native-seams.json
provider-neutral settings state until a narrower accepted route exists
dependencies.plannedAction: retain only for accepted additive/wrapper seams; remove if every consumer migrates to a narrower official route
dependencies.rationale: Current runtime relies on additive/wrapper annotations. Replacing whole vanilla REDmod script files for the same hooks would increase conflict and patch surface.

dependencies.plannedAction: remove when the presentation/settings lane supplies the accepted Biology-owned/provider-neutral preference surface
dependencies.rationale: The product requires at most a tiny settings contract; Mod Settings is a provider, not simulation authority, and currently creates dependency depth without another Biology consumer.

dependencies.plannedAction: remove with Mod Settings unless a separate final Biology resource feature proves a direct requirement
dependencies.rationale: No project-original source/resource in the canonical tree currently consumes ArchiveXL directly.

consumerFeatures: transitional dependency chain for ArchiveXL/Mod Settings
dependencies.plannedAction: remove if ArchiveXL/Mod Settings are removed and no concrete Biology-owned native plugin consumer is demonstrated
dependencies.rationale: The canonical project has REDscript source but no Biology-owned RED4ext DLL/plugin consumer. Historical presence alone is not a retention reason.
No current Biology production source/data path requires TweakXL; REDmod-native tweak source is preferred if future tweak content is needed.
Current Biology Ink/REDscript source has no Codeware dependency.
Biology currently defines no custom input binding that requires Input Loader.
Finished Biology gameplay must be project-owned.
Finished Biology presentation must be project-owned.

dependencies.plannedAction: read/reference only through supported game install; never redistribute
dependencies.rationale: Biology targets the installed game and may not redistribute CDPR executables, archives, scripts, saves, or generated stock caches.

rules: A dependency without at least one concrete current Biology consumer is not retained.
A parallel lane requesting a new dependency must identify the exact feature, why vanilla/REDmod/current redscript cannot satisfy it, and the package/install consequence before this graph changes.

Removal-candidate does not mean delete the framework from a currently tested transitional build before its consumer is migrated; it means it is not part of the accepted REDmod-first target without new evidence.
Bundled third-party components require pinned version/hash/license/provenance before release.
